foods_to_include: Whole Grains: Oats, quinoa, brown rice, whole-wheat bread/pasta, barley, farro

Lean Proteins: Skinless poultry, fish (especially fatty fish like salmon, mackerel, sardines for omega-3s and Vitamin D), lean cuts of beef/pork (in moderation), eggs, tofu, tempeh, lentils, beans, chickpeas
Healthy Fats: Avocados, nuts (almonds, walnuts, pecans), seeds (chia seeds, flax seeds, hemp seeds), olive oil, avocado oil
Fruits: Berries, apples, pears, oranges, grapefruit (whole fruits preferred over juices)
Vegetables: A wide variety of non-starchy vegetables including leafy greens (spinach, kale), broccoli, cauliflower, bell peppers, zucchini, tomatoes, cucumbers
Dairy/Alternatives: Low-fat milk, fortified plant-based milk alternatives (almond, soy), low-fat yogurt (plain, unsweetened)
Vitamin D-Rich Foods: Fatty fish, fortified milk/plant milks, fortified cereals
Fiber-Rich Foods: All whole grains, fruits, vegetables, legumes, nuts, seeds
foods_to_avoid: Refined Sugars: Sugary drinks, candies, pastries, desserts, sweetened yogurts, fruit juices with added sugar
Processed Foods: Packaged snacks, fast food, processed meats, most frozen meals
Saturated Fats: High-fat red meats, full-fat dairy products (butter, cheese), coconut oil, palm oil, fried foods
Trans Fats: Margarine, commercially baked goods, many processed snack foods (check labels for 'partially hydrogenated oils')
Refined Grains: White bread, white pasta, white rice, sugary breakfast cereals
Excessive Sodium: High-sodium processed foods, canned soups, cured meats

lifestyle_advice: **Hydration:** Maintain adequate hydration by drinking plenty of water throughout the day. Aim for at least 8-10 glasses (approximately 2-2.5 liters) daily, more if exercising or in a hot climate.

**Regular Physical Activity:** Continue your moderately active lifestyle and consider incorporating a mix of cardiovascular exercises (e.g., brisk walking, jogging, cycling) and strength training (e.g., bodyweight exercises, lifting weights) at least 3-5 times per week. Physical activity can significantly help improve glucose control, raise HDL, and lower triglycerides.
**Adequate Sleep:** Aim for 7-9 hours of quality sleep per night. Poor sleep can impact blood sugar regulation and overall metabolic health.

**Stress Management:** Incorporate stress-reducing activities into your daily routine, such as meditation, yoga, deep breathing exercises, or spending time in nature, as stress can influence hormone levels and metabolic function.

**Safe Sun Exposure for Vitamin D:** If feasible and safe for your skin type, brief, regular sun exposure (e.g., 10-15 minutes, 2-3 times a week, avoiding peak sun hours) may help improve Vitamin D levels. Always prioritize sun safety and discuss this with your healthcare provider, especially if you have fair skin or a history of skin concerns.
